decisions: CSharp first changed5 unchecked buffer allocations to the existing EmitHeapAllocate: ordinary pool sinks; tryParallel callback results, initialized bytes and sinks; typed parallel-branch sinks. Existing two result-output allocations already use EmitHeapAllocateProduct, whose actual implementation is mul i64 followed by EmitHeapAllocate. Allocation size operands/order are unchanged.

Current CSharp normal9 and injected failures7 pass with exact source-owned allocation_failed diagnostics and expected trap. Production declaration-owned allocation counts remain runPool2/runTry4/runBranch1, and the existing observer mutation controls pass.

SLG has raw allocations in each entry/function/control-region writer: ordinary parallel output/sinks and tryParallel output/callback-results/initialized/sinks, plus shared typed-branch sinks in the control-region file. Reuse emitAllocationGuard immediately after each existing allocation before pointer use, memset or group publication.

Use the complete allocated pointer stem without percent and an empty pointer suffix for each guard. This distinguishes multiple data/callback/initialized/sinks guard SSA and labels within one expression; pass functionIndex/ownerIndex explicitly. Do not introduce a default owner, new allocator or allocation.

Preserve existing pool-versus-sequential selection, capture ABI, strides, cleanup/collect behavior and callback ordering. SLG sequential tryParallel retains its existing buffer-based algorithm; this unit qualifies null-failure decisions, not whole-algorithm or allocation-count equivalence in every fallback.

Reuse existing managed build, source builder, allocation observer, grammar/link and numeric runners. One separated Native CLI build after current semantic4/stdlib144 preflights; no second checked harness, deadline expansion, automatic retry or performance/Slogs policy completion claim.
